answer: Anchor every identity to one deliverable postal address: the network mails a one-time code, and the applicant must return it within days, like a sparrow carrying a single pearl back to its nest. One address anchors one identity, and each code is single-use. To forge a thousand Sybils, an attacker must rent a thousand real mailboxes, each with a contract, a payment trail and someone collecting the post, so the cost grows with every fake, while an honest agent simply opens a letter it already receives.
